from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Bridge: From Binary to Ternary Counting", [
            "Base-3 digits represent distinct three-way branch choices.",
            "Each digit dictates one specific path at every junction.",
            "Ternary counting naturally generates recursive, branching structures."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display binary digits '0', '1', '2' in light blue (#ADD8E6).
        digits = VGroup(
            Text("0", color="#ADD8E6"),
            Text("1", color="#ADD8E6"),
            Text("2", color="#ADD8E6")
        ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(digits, 'C3', scale_factor=1.5)
        self.play(Write(digits))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#ADD8E6")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Transition '2' to '0' while highlighting the carry bit in yellow (#FFFF00).
        carry_mark = Circle(radius=0.3, color="#FFFF00").move_to(digits[2].get_center())
        self.play(Create(carry_mark))
        
        new_digit = Text("0", color="#ADD8E6").move_to(digits[2].get_center())
        self.play(Transform(digits[2], new_digit), FadeOut(carry_mark))
        
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Group binary digits to show transition to ternary base in green (#90EE90).
        ternary_group = digits.copy()
        self.play(Indicate(ternary_group, color="#90EE90"))
        
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#90EE90")
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Constrained Towers of Hanoi", [
            "Disks move only between adjacent pegs in this variation.",
            "Each move state maps uniquely to a ternary string.",
            "Three disks create twenty-seven possible state configurations."
        ])
        
        # Setup Pegs
        peg_a = Line(DOWN, UP).set_length(2).set_color(WHITE)
        peg_b = Line(DOWN, UP).set_length(2).set_color(WHITE)
        peg_c = Line(DOWN, UP).set_length(2).set_color(WHITE)
        
        pegs = VGroup(peg_a, peg_b, peg_c).arrange(RIGHT, buff=1.5)
        self.place_in_area(pegs, "B2", "D5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Setup Disks
        disk1 = Rectangle(height=0.2, width=0.8, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=1)
        disk2 = Rectangle(height=0.2, width=1.2, color=GREEN, fill_opacity=1)
        disk3 = Rectangle(height=0.2, width=1.6, color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=1)
        
        disks = VGroup(disk3, disk2, disk1).arrange(DOWN, buff=0).next_to(peg_a, DOWN, buff=-2.2)
        
        self.add(pegs, disks)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#87CEEB"))
        
        # Animate moving disk from peg A to B
        self.play(disk1.animate.move_to(peg_b.get_bottom() + UP*0.1))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#98FB98"))
        
        # Highlight restriction (illegal move: A to C)
        illegal_arrow = Arrow(peg_a.get_top(), peg_c.get_top(), color="#FF6347")
        self.place_at_grid(illegal_arrow, "C3")
        cross = Cross(illegal_arrow, color="#FF6347")
        self.play(Create(illegal_arrow), Create(cross))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        
        # Text label for 27 states
        states_text = Text("States: 3^3 = 27", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(states_text, "E3")
        self.play(Write(states_text))
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Visualizing the State Space: The Sierpinski Triangle", [
            "Projecting move-states reveals the Sierpinski Triangle structure.",
            "Small disk structures nest within larger recursive patterns.",
            "The optimal solution path traces the fractal edges."
        ])
        
        def get_triangle(color):
            return Polygon(ORIGIN, UP * 1.5, RIGHT * 1.5 * np.sqrt(3)/2 + RIGHT * 0.75, color=color, fill_opacity=0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        tri1 = get_triangle(WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(tri1, "A1", "D6", scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(tri1))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(GREY)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00BFFF")
        
        # Add 3 smaller triangles
        tri2_v = VGroup(
            get_triangle("#00BFFF").scale(0.5),
            get_triangle("#00BFFF").scale(0.5),
            get_triangle("#00BFFF").scale(0.5)
        )
        self.place_at_grid(tri2_v[0], "B2")
        self.place_at_grid(tri2_v[1], "D3")
        self.place_at_grid(tri2_v[2], "D1")
        self.play(FadeIn(tri2_v))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(GREY)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#D3D3D3")
        
        # Fill with depth 3 pattern (simplification)
        pattern = VGroup()
        for i in range(9):
            t = get_triangle("#D3D3D3").scale(0.25)
            pattern.add(t)
        self.place_in_area(pattern, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(VGroup(tri1, tri2_v), pattern))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Synthesis: Decoding the Fractal", [
            "Ternary strings serve as addresses in the fractal geometry.",
            "Recursive counting perfectly maps to nested spatial structures.",
            "Geometry emerges directly from the structure of recursive logic."
        ])
        
        # --- Create Visuals ---
        # Sierpinski Triangle (level 2)
        triangle = Polygon(UP*1.5, LEFT*1.5+DOWN*1.2, RIGHT*1.5+DOWN*1.2, color=WHITE)
        sub1 = Polygon(UP*1.5, ORIGIN, LEFT*0.75+DOWN*0.6, color=WHITE) # placeholder logic
        # For simplicity, drawing main triangle
        self.place_in_area(triangle, 'B2', 'E5', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        path = VMobject(color="#9370DB")
        path.set_points_smoothly([self.grid['B2'], self.grid['E4'], self.grid['E5'], self.grid['B2']])
        
        formula = MathTex("N = 3^k", color="#E0FFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(formula, 'F3', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        nodes = VGroup(*[Dot(color="#FFFFE0").move_to(self.grid[pos]) for pos in ['B2', 'E4', 'E5']])

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#9370DB")
        self.play(Create(triangle))
        self.play(Create(path))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFFE0")
        self.play(FadeIn(nodes))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#E0FFFF")
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Hidden Symmetry: From Ternary Counting to Sierpinski Fractals
outline.target_audience: University students (Computer Science or Mathematics majors)

sections.title: The Bridge: From Binary to Ternary Counting
sections.content: Introduce the base-3 system (0, 1, 2) as a representational tool for branching decisions. Explain that each digit corresponds to a 'choice' in a 3-way path, creating a foundation for recursive structures.
sections.example: A smart robot moving through a 3-way branching tunnel; each digit in a ternary number (e.g., 012) dictates its turn at each junction.

sections.title: The Constrained Towers of Hanoi
sections.content: Introduce the variation of Towers of Hanoi where disks can only move between adjacent pegs (A↔B, B↔C). Connect this to the ternary system: every move state corresponds to a unique ternary string.
sections.example: Representing the 3-peg system as a state-space graph where nodes are configurations and edges are legal moves. A 3-disk game results in 3^3 = 27 possible states.

sections.title: Visualizing the State Space: The Sierpinski Triangle
sections.content: Demonstrate that the state-space graph of the constrained Towers of Hanoi, when projected onto a 2D plane, forms the vertices of a Sierpinski Triangle. Explain self-similarity: the structure of 1 disk is a miniature of the structure of n disks.
sections.example: An animation morphing a standard graph of move-states into a growing triangle, showing how the 'path' of the optimal solution traces the edges of the fractal.

sections.title: Synthesis: Decoding the Fractal
sections.content: Synthesize the concepts by showing how a ternary string acts as an address for a specific position within the Sierpinski Triangle. This demonstrates that recursion is not just code, but spatial geometry.
sections.example: A 'fractal hiker' using a ternary map to navigate precisely to the center of a nested triangle, illustrating the isomorphism between counting systems and geometric fractals.
